review_notes:
I read all of UniformBasepointHeight.lean. I also read the related CenteredHeightError.lean and grepped the repo for repeated fragments. The three theorems prove different things:
- `uniform_sublinear_height_of_stable_labels` reduces to existing helper lemmas, `stable_label_independent_of_center` and `uniform_local_norm_bound_of_sequences`.
- `uniform_sublinear_of_local_radius_bound` is a radius-shifting estimate.
- `centered_uniform_height_of_two_point_estimate` is a rewrite using `map_mul`/`map_inv` and an isometry step.
The only repeated piece found is the one-line fact `dist x (x * g) = dist 1 g` via `dist_mul_left`. It appears here at line 89, in CenteredHeightError.lean line 34, and in MetricFolnerUnimodular.lean line 40. That is a short routine step, so it is not repeated proof machinery under this rubric. `centered_height_sublinear` in CenteredHeightError.lean has a different proof, because it re-centers a one-point estimate and needs a triangle inequality. I found no shared nontrivial reasoning that would justify a new lemma.
